REUTERS: Mexico Expects Economy to Outperform IMF Projections
July 8, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Straight reporting, no editorializing: Reuters runs Finance Minister Edgar Amador's line that Mexico will beat the IMF's downgraded 1.2% growth forecast for 2026.

🇲🇽 Amador ties the IMF's cut to "the shock to the energy market caused by tensions in the Persian Gulf" — a global revision, not a Mexican policy failure. Worth noting when the coverage is actually fair.

• "a global downward revision to the IMF's estimates for world economies"

CNN: Mexico-US Relations Are Strained — and "About to Get Worse"
July 12, 2026 | 🟡

📰 CNN's read on Sheinbaum seeking charges over Mexicans killed in US custody: an analyst calls it "a performance" and says "the opportunity to take these issues seriously is lost."

🔍 The piece repeats ICE's "rammed a vehicle" line, frames both governments as equally to blame for a "very damaged" relationship, and quotes no migrant-advocacy or Mexican civil-society voices.

• "It's a performance. The opportunity to take these issues seriously is lost"
• "There are no signs of rebuilding the relationship; the relationship is very damaged"

FOX NEWS: Mexico Vows US Will Pay After ICE Shoots "Illegal Migrant" Who "Rammed" Agent
July 10, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Fox labels Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52 — a Houston man who lived in the US for decades and was driving workers to a jobsite — an "illegal migrant" who "weaponized his vehicle." 🔍 The agents who killed him had no body cameras.

ICE's account runs as fact; Fox notes Sheinbaum's demands would have "no legal effect in U.S. courts." A line it buried is Mexico's own: "His story is the embodiment of what it means to seek the American Dream."

• "refused to follow multiple verbal commands, and weaponized his vehicle"
• "We cannot tolerate the mistreatment of our fellow citizens... in the United States"

🇲🇽🌎 <u>8 OF 10 MEXICAN-MADE CARS GO TO ONE BUYER — AND JUNE SHOWED THE RISK</u>

Mexican auto exports fell 9.2% in June (INEGI, via El Financiero), with the US still absorbing 75.9% of shipments in the first half of the year. UNAM economist Raúl Vázquez López calls that concentration a structural vulnerability: "A more diversified pattern would strengthen us," he argues, urging Mexico to redirect trade toward Latin America, Europe and Asia. It's the exact dependence Sheinbaum's diversification drive — new deals with the EU, China and across Latin America — is built to unwind.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S REAL WAGES ROSE 15% WHILE US AND CANADIAN WAGES SHRANK</u>

While workers in the US and Canada both saw real wages fall in 2026, Mexican workers' real wages have climbed 15.1% since 2021 — triple the OECD average of 4.9%, and second in the world only to Slovenia. The OECD credits the minimum-wage policy, up nearly 30 points over the period, plus labor productivity gains running above anything seen since the mid-1990s. Raising the minimum wage every year, the thing they said would wreck the economy.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>4T TO EL UNIVERSAL AND EL FINANCIERO: YOUR ROCHA MOYA STORY IS "ABSOLUTELY FALSE"</u>

Mexico's Security Cabinet flatly rejected reports by El Universal and El Financiero claiming Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya is being sheltered under military guard in the 9th Military Zone — "absolutely false," it said, stressing the government protects no one under investigation and applies a "zero-impunity strategy without distinction." The record backs the posture: 56,000 arrests for serious crimes under Sheinbaum, 87 officials detained in Operation Enjambre (7 of them sitting mayors), and homicides down 46% — 39 fewer killings a day since September 2024.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>WASHINGTON POST VIDEOS GUT ICE'S "SELF-DEFENSE" STORY IN HOUSTON</u>

Surveillance footage analyzed by the Washington Post shows ICE agents in unmarked cars chasing Lorenzo Salgado Araujo through Houston — and never shows him trying to ram anyone, directly contradicting DHS's claim its agent fired "in self-defense." Three men detained in the same raid say the officer opened fire almost the instant he stepped out of his vehicle, and that the driver never veered toward him. This is the killing Washington called self-defense.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>EX-DEA CHIEF TELLS MEXICO TO INVITE US TROOPS IN</u>

Derek Maltz, former acting head of the DEA, publicly called on Mexico to join Washington's hemispheric "anti-cartel coalition" and to request US military forces on its own soil. It lands as the Trump administration pushes Latin America to accept joint operations inside its borders — the exact thing Sheinbaum has refused, again and again, under one principle: coordination without subordination.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>DUTCH TRADER VITOL BRIBED A PEMEX DIRECTOR — $400K, PEÑA NIETO ERA</u>

Contralínea puts a name to the Vitol bribery scheme: Luis Rafael Montanaro Sánchez, head of Pemex Etileno from 2016 to 2018, negotiating "agreements" over WhatsApp with Vitol's representative on trips to Houston. Vitol admitted in US court to roughly $400,000 in bribes to Mexican officials — part of a $10 million Latin American scheme — and paid Washington $163 million. It offered Mexico $30 million; Mexico won't take it until every official is named.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>CNI REPORT: DEA KIDNAPPED "EL MAYO" ON MEXICAN SOIL</u>

A CNI intelligence report confirms what Washington denied for a year: Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada was seized on Mexican territory. At the moment of his capture he phoned family to say DEA agents had detained him "as a result of a pact." Ex-ambassador Ken Salazar swore in August 2024 that no US agents took part — the FGR now calls that "completely false."
